title: The server saves its workspaces and restores them at start
body:
A session should mostly survive a reboot. Today nothing about the layout is saved.

## Proposal

The server saves each workspace's layout, its panes' labels and cwds after changes, before a pane exits and at shutdown. At start it restores them. Terminal panes restart in their cwd, and GUI panes come back empty, with a way to relaunch them to follow later. The saved file is an on-disk format with a version byte under CLAUDE.md.

decade-cc25be, what replaces anchors and pinning, needs settling before this, because it decides what a saved pane holds.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6b9cbed5
notes.text: decade-cc25be is decided. A saved pane holds a name, a command or a plain shell, and a cwd. GUI apps are not relaunched, which is decade-15e5eb. Whether a GUI pane comes back as an empty slot is open here.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6b9cbed5
notes.text:
Jack approved the proposal Claude made for this issue:

- The file is `~/.local/state/decade/workspaces.toml`, with `version = 1`. A version key satisfies the version-byte rule in CLAUDE.md.
- It holds each workspace in picker order (name, cwd, focused pane, zoom, split tree with ratios) and each pane (name, pinned, cwd for a terminal, app id for a GUI app).
- A terminal pane's cwd is the live cwd of the shell under its ghostty, read from `/proc/<shell pid>/cwd`. The shell is a child of the ghostty process.
- decade saves 1 s after a change, every 60 s, and on SIGTERM before it kills its children.
- At start, decade rebuilds each workspace and starts a plain shell in ghostty in each terminal pane's cwd. Running programs such as coax or nvim are not resumed.
- A GUI pane comes back as an empty slot, which a window with its app id fills again. Relaunching is decade-15e5eb.
- A file decade cannot read is logged and left alone, and decade starts fresh without saving over it.
- There is no flag to start without restoring.
- The pin change (decade-7c65be) stays separate. The file records only whether a pane is pinned.
